name: wilkinson-tree
prompt: fixture_wilkinson_tree.py wires a 1:4 Wilkinson divider tree with no geometry: a WilkinsonCell circuit (one 1:2 divider and its 100 ohm isolation resistor), a WilkinsonTree circuit of three cells (first feeding second[0] and second[1]), and a WilkinsonBoard with the input SMA jack j_in on the left edge and four output jacks j_out[0..3] on the right edge, 25 mm apart, matched by its timing constraint (each output path within 1.0 ps of output 0's). Lay it out in code for 2.45 GHz. Draw each divider's copper in WilkinsonCell, so all three cells share it: one OverlappableCopper body on L1 with 0.30 mm input and output stubs, each at least 0.3 mm long, and two arms of the fixture's ARM_71 width, 0.17 mm, each a quarter wavelength long at 2.45 GHz on ARM_71's velocity of 1.6e11 mm/s (within 0.5 mm), the isolation resistor across the arm ends. An arm's length is its centre line between the 0.30 mm copper it leaves and the 0.30 mm copper it reaches, and each arm meets that copper square on, its end across the arm, with no fillet where an arm meets the 0.30 mm copper, and the two arms touch each other nowhere but where they leave the 0.30 mm copper. Draw no other copper but the tangency squares below. Pour GND on L1 around the bodies, and put a pour and via KeepOut on the body's outline grown by 0.20 mm, the clearance the fixture's ARM_71 and the substrate's CPWG_50_FENCED declare, so the pour stands 0.20 mm off the body (up to 0.03 mm more is fine). Fence each body as a region on GND whose fence region is the body copper itself, so its two rows of fence vias at 1.0 mm pitch stand 0.6 mm and 1.2 mm off the body's copper edge, as the line's do. Keep fence vias and the pour 0.20 mm off the isolation resistor with a pour and via KeepOut on the rectangle over its two pads and the gap between them, grown by 0.20 mm, so no pour runs between the isolation pads, and put no other via keepout near the bodies or along the RF lines (a launch cutout under a jack's centre pad is fine within 0.9 mm of the line's axis, from the board edge to 2.0 mm past the pad's inner end). A route KeepOut over the body may keep routes off it, but it must stop short of the cell's port pads. The first row must be full all the way round, the inside of the loop between the arms included: every stretch of it farther than 1.85 mm from a route's centre line (the line fence's outer row, 1.35 mm off it, plus the 0.5 mm between via centres that the fab sheet's 0.25 mm drill and 0.25 mm hole-to-hole space set) and 0.45 mm from a resistor pad (its 0.20 mm plus a 0.25 mm via pad radius) holds a via every 1.0 mm. Report the outer row as read back. Run the input feed, the two joins between cells and the four output feeds as CPWG_50_FENCED with its two rows of fence vias. The straight exits of a cell's three ports (each from the end of the port's stub along its axis to its square's far edge) stand at least 3.2 mm apart at their closest, whichever way they point. That one floor holds for every pair; two lines leaving side by side set it, since each line's outer fence row stands 1.35 mm off its centre line and the fab sheet puts via centres at least 0.5 mm apart, so at 3.2 each keeps both fence rows. Every route leaves or reaches a jack's centre pad or a cell port straight along its axis to a RoutePoint 2.0 to 3.0 mm out, measured from the end of the body's 0.30 mm stub at a cell port and from the inner end of the centre pad at a jack. At each of those RoutePoints, at every jack and every cell port, draw one 0.20 mm square of GND Copper on L1 on the inside of the turn that follows, from the RoutePoint to 0.20 mm past it, its near side 1.0 mm off the trace's copper edge (1.15 mm off the axis); on the input feed, which runs straight on, either side will do. Tag the squares and the RF nets and declare a design_constraint clearance of 1.0 mm between the tags, so the line holds the axis through the square's far edge and bends around its corner on a centre-line radius of 1.15 mm (half the 0.30 trace plus the 1.0). No RF copper may come within 1.0 mm of any square. A route with Route.Config(envelope_overhead) does not keep that clearance (its copper can reach tagged copper with no issue reported), so the envelope route must start and end clear of the squares. Match the outputs by the timing constraint: each join and each output feed runs as a straight exit to the tangency RoutePoint, a plain route around the square to a second RoutePoint clear of it (3.0 mm on, at 45 degrees off the axis toward the turn, clears it), the one route carrying Route.Config(envelope_overhead=E) with E no more than 3.0 mm, then the same plain bend and straight entry at the far end: at most five routes, and every route but the envelope one no longer than 4.0 mm along its centre line. The input feed is common to every path and stays straight, with no envelope; its two ends are the only ones where the line runs straight on past its square instead of bending around it. The build must report every skew within the constraint's 1.0 ps and no unmet timing. Keep the fixture's circuits, ports, connectors, nets and timing constraint, and its class names.
notes: The fixture module is fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, Design WilkinsonTreeDesign. It imports the Würth 60312202114514 jack from jitxexamples and no jitxexamples.patterns module; the isolation resistor is fictional and needs no parts database. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.wilkinson_tree (py-components 95c54da): its numbers (5.8 GHz, effective permittivity 4.4, 0.18 mm arms, so 6.16 mm arms; 20 mm output pitch; its own board and sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, so a copied example fails the arm length and does not fit the fixture's jacks. The quarter wave is 1.6e11 / 2.45e9 / 4 = 16.327 mm. The prompt fixes where an arm is measured (its centre line between the 0.30 copper it joins, met square on, with no fillet, the arms touching nowhere but where they leave that copper) so the check can read it from the body's area: an opening by 0.12 mm with square corners keeps the 0.30 copper and drops the 0.17 arms, the arm copper within 0.1 mm of the wide copper is cut so arms that touch at the junction part, and each arm's area over 0.17 plus what the same reading drops from a straight arm of known length between two square joins (worked in the check, 0.2000) is its length. Worked in shapely with the check's own reading on arms drawn at 16.327: butt and T joins read 16.327, the base body 16.326, arms touching side by side at a stub's end face 16.327. A round opening read T joins about 0.03 long per join and the base body 16.382. Arms that overlap where they leave the stub, or run side by side along a stretch, form copper as wide as the stub that no width reading separates (with square corners, arms that overlap, or run side by side for 0.3 or 1.0 mm before curving apart, fuse into one piece read at 31.4 to 32.8; a round opening read overlaps of 0.02 to 0.04 at 15.692 to 16.069); the prompt rules both out, since over that stretch they are one wider line, not two arms. A 0.30 stub shorter than about 0.25 mm vanishes in the 0.12 opening and is read as arm (0.24 mm reads 17.374 for an arm drawn at 16.327), so the prompt asks for stubs at least 0.3 mm long. Fillets misread (fillets of 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 mm on a 10.0 arm read 9.738, 9.626 and 10.01), so the prompt rules them out and the reading has one definition. An earlier base drew the arcs from the stub's centre line into the stubs and read 16.137 for arcs drawn at 16.327. Findings from the base solution: a route KeepOut over the body that also covers the cell's port pads leaves every route from those pads unrouted ('Unable to find path', 9 routes); stopping the route keepout short of each port pad (the pour keepout can still cover the whole body) fixes it. Routes ending on a port pad can realize as polygon traces with no width; the check reads such a trace's width as the short side of its minimum rotated rectangle. The region fence worked as a fence-tagged L1 Pour declared in WilkinsonCell on the cell's own GND net, with the design_constraint(tag).fence_via rule declared in WilkinsonBoard; the known submit error for a fence-tagged child pour joined to a parent's net ('Key N does not exist in table', ticket 50813757593) did not arise, so the region fence is in the deterministic check. Inside the body's own pour keepout the L1 fence pour realizes Empty and capture keeps no shape for it, but its fence stands; the check reads the region from the first row on either layer: each via must stand within 0.02 of the body copper offset by 0.6, round or mitred (0.02 holds an arc-drawn body, whose captured chords stand up to 0.005 either side of the arc; base: 58 vias per body read 0.6000 to 0.6446 off the copper, each 0.0000 off one of those offsets; the Sonnet run's 59 read 0.6000 to 0.7285, also 0.0000 off). A test on only the nearest and the median via passed a region grown on part of its outline (the variant below read 0.6000 to 0.8000, median 0.6000). The same pour on L2 also passes (it realizes as the body copper, 0.0363 mm2 apart, and its vias read as on L1). A BridgingPinModel from the cell's input port to each output port (delay from the drawn length over the velocity) lets the board's constraint resolve through the cells; with it the report shows three UnmetTimeDiff measurements, each carrying its own satisfied flag; the check reads them from rd.issues(satisfied=True), which lists met and unmet groups alike, and fails any over 1.0 ps. IssueReport.text() prints category names ('Signal Constraint'), not class names, so the unmet report is also read for 'signal constraint'. Tangency squares: a GND Copper square tagged for a 1.0 mm clearance to the RF tag sets the bend on a plain route (radius 0.15 + 1.0, measured on the rf-connector-launch base), but a route with envelope_overhead ignores it: with the envelope route starting at the tangency RoutePoint (EW2's sections), its copper came 0.0062 to 0.89 from the squares at 12 of the 14 ends, the line left the axis before the squares' far edges, and the build reported no issue and every skew met (0.990 ps). Hence the plain bend to a second RoutePoint before the envelope route. With that bend (3.0 mm on at 45 degrees), every square read 1.0000 from the routed copper (0.9854 as a polygon where the line bends, the arc flattening the rf case's notes explain), each bend an arc of 1.15 centred on its square's corner, and the skews 0.990, 0.990 and 0.990 ps at E = 3.0. The five-route and 4.0 mm limits follow from that shape: exit, bend, envelope route, bend, entry, with exits of 2.0 to 2.15 (the cell RoutePoints stand 2.15 past the stub end, the jack ones 2.0 past the pad) and bends whose chord is 3.0. With each second RoutePoint on the axis instead of 45 degrees off it, every route stays short and every square keeps its clearance, but the line runs straight on past the squares; only the input feed's two ends may do that. Region fence and the hull keepout: an earlier base also put a via KeepOut on the convex hull of the body and the resistor pads; with it the first row inside the loop held 0 vias on its 28.140 mm stretch, a gap of the whole stretch. Without it, per body, the first row read 29 vias inside the loop (room for 27 on 28.140 mm, widest gap 1.031) and 33 serving the four stretches outside it (widest gap 0.993 on the two 13.732 mm stretches); the outer row read 4 inside (room for 26 on 27.181 mm) and 7 outside (room for 27 on 31.493 mm). A build with via=False on the body's own keepout read the outer row the same (4 inside, 7 outside on the first body), so the body keepout does not thin it, and the fence pour on L1 read it the same as on L2; a 2026-11-06 Sonnet run's layout with the same fence_via rule read 20 inside and 35 outside, so the body or route geometry thins it; with the region pattern's pitch at 1.2 and 1.5 the base's outer row on the first body read 4 inside and 5 outside, and 6 and 5, so the pitch alone does not explain it; the cause is not found, and the prompt asks only that the outer row be reported as read back. The Sonnet run put each cell's two output stubs 1.2 mm apart: the exit check read the neighbouring line as stray copper, and the two lines' fence rows overlap, so the prompt asks for 3.2 mm between a cell's straight exits at their closest, whichever way they point, one floor set by two lines leaving side by side (two outer rows of 1.35 plus the 0.5 via spacing), and the check fails 'straight exits 1.200 apart at their closest, under 3.20'; the base's outputs leave in opposite directions, 5.6 apart, and its input stands 13.952 from each. Between a cell's output legs the first row passes itself 0.1 apart, and the router puts that stretch's vias on one side of it, so a via serves any stretch within 0.5 of it (no second via can stand there); two 1.921 mm stretches there hold no via by the count rule and are not scored. The 1.85 route exclusion is derived (outer line row 1.35 plus the 0.5 via centre spacing from fab sheet rows 12 and 15), replacing an earlier 2.0 that had no source. A via keepout around each tangency square, which a runner might add to keep vias off the bends, sits inside the line's fence band and eats it at every bend; the check fails any via keepout near the bodies or the RF lines past the two the prompt names and the bounded launch cutout. The resistor keepout covers the gap between the isolation pads too: grown around each pad alone it let the L1 pour into that 0.4 mm gap, 0.1958 from the body. The prompt's 'so no pour runs between the isolation pads' is not scored by the check (that sliver reads inside the 0.19 pour gap bound) or named in a judge assertion. Base solution readback: L1 pour 0.199 mm off each body (the keepout grown by 0.20, read 0.001 inside it) and over none of it; the check's 0.19 lower bound allows the chord sag of a coarse round buffer (0.004 at four segments a quarter circle) and still fails a pour on the bare outline or at half the clearance; route fence rows at 0.75 and 1.35 off the centre lines; seven pieces of routed copper, each matched piece with five routes and one envelope; arms 16.326. Wrong variants (each fails the check for its own reason): a meander drawn as Copper in the tree in place of one join's middle route fails 'copper drawn outside a cell' (and, because the router does not count the drawn copper as joining the join's two routes, five more lines: piece count, two envelope counts, 'No path for signal constraint' and no skew measurements); a zigzag of four RoutePoints in one join, with no envelope there, fails 'a 4.327 mm route with no envelope on a matched section, over 4.0' (the router runs each leg between RoutePoints straight, so the legs fail by length and the envelope count, not by bends); a body KeepOut without pour=True fails 'L1 pour covers 7.2063 mm2 of the body' and 'no pour KeepOut over 7.5303 mm2 of the body'; a pour KeepOut on the bare body outline fails 'L1 pour covers 0.0106 mm2 of the body' and 'L1 pour stands 0.000 off the body, not 0.19 to 0.23'; a pour KeepOut on the outline grown by 0.10 overlaps nothing and fails only 'L1 pour stands 0.098 off the body, not 0.19 to 0.23'; no region fence fails 'no fence-tagged shape over the body, so no region fence'; the fence pour on the body outline grown by 0.20 fails 'the fence region is not the body copper: 58 of 58 first-row vias stand off the copper's 0.6 offset by over 0.02'; the same pour grown by 0.20 only above y = 2.0 fails it with 25 of 57; the hull via keepout restored fails 'the first row inside the loop has a 28.140 mm gap on a 28.140 mm free stretch, over 1.5'; a via keepout grown 0.4 around each tangency square fails 'a via KeepOut on layer 0 ... reaches 0.8618 mm2 past the body and the resistor's pad rectangle grown by 0.2'; an 8.0 by 3.2 via keepout centred on each jack at the board edge (over the centre pad, 0.7 mm wider than the launch cutout on each side) fails 'a via KeepOut on layer 1 ... reaches 12.8782 mm2 past' the same allowance; each second RoutePoint on the axis fails 'no bend of radius 1.15 centred on the tangency square's corner'; the envelope route started at the tangency RoutePoint fails 'the line does not hold the axis from the port through the square's far edge' and the square clearance; bodies drawn in tree containers instead of the cell fail 'copper drawn outside a cell'; envelopes of 0.05 mm fail 'skew 24.685 ps over the prompt's 1.0 ps'. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its class names (WilkinsonCell, WilkinsonTree, WilkinsonBoard, WilkinsonTreeDesign). Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors, nets or timing constraint, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: WilkinsonCell draws one OverlappableCopper body (0.30 stubs, two 0.17 arms of 16.33 mm meeting the stubs square on), a pour and via KeepOut on its outline grown by 0.20, a route KeepOut over it short of the port pads, a fence-tagged GND pour on L1 (or L2) equal to the body copper for the region fence (on L1 it realizes Empty inside the body keepout and its fence stands), a pour and via KeepOut on the rectangle over the isolation resistor's pads and the gap between them, grown by 0.20, a tagged 0.20 mm GND Copper square at each of its three ports, and port pads the routes can end on, its straight exits at least 3.2 mm apart at their closest (the base's outputs leave in opposite directions, 5.6 apart), so the three cells share it; WilkinsonTree places the cells and holds the join sections; WilkinsonBoard applies CPWG_50_FENCED to the RF nets, declares the region fence_via rule and the 1.0 mm clearance between the square tag and the RF tag, draws a tagged square at each jack, pours GND on L1 and L2, and routes the input feed and output feeds; each join and output feed is a straight exit to a RoutePoint 2.0 to 3.0 mm out on the port axis, a plain bend around the square to a second RoutePoint clear of it, one route with Route.Config(envelope_overhead) of 3.0 mm or less, and the mirrored bend and straight entry; no hull or ring keepout around the body; the build reports each skew within 1.0 ps; COMPLETION.md with the arm lengths, the pour gap to each body, the region fence vias by row, the exits, the bends and the gap to each square, and the skews read back.

assertions.text: three WilkinsonCell instances under the one WilkinsonTree, each with one OverlappableCopper body on L1 and no copper drawn anywhere else but the 0.20 mm tangency squares; two 0.17 arms per body each a quarter wave at 2.45 GHz on 1.6e11 mm/s within 0.5 mm, measured between the 0.30 copper they meet square on; an L1 GND pour around each body, over none of it and 0.19 to 0.23 off it (the prompt's 0.20, less 0.01 for a coarse buffer's chord sag), with a pour KeepOut covering each body; the region fence's tagged shape is the body copper, and each stretch of the first row (0.6 off the copper, inside the loop and outside it) at least 2.0 long, more than 1.85 from a route centre line and 0.45 from a resistor pad, has no gap over 1.5 among the vias within 0.5 of it; no via KeepOut near the bodies or the RF lines reaches past the body and the rectangle over the resistor pads, each grown by 0.20, and a launch cutout within 0.9 of a jack's axis from the board edge to 2.0 past its centre pad; every route on L1 at 0.30 with the fence in two rows; at each of the nine cell ports and five jacks one 0.20 mm GND copper square 2.0 to 3.0 out from the stub end or jack pad and 1.15 off the axis, the line on the axis through its far edge and then bent on a 1.15 radius centred on its corner (straight on only at the input feed's two ends), no routed copper within 1.0 of any square read from the centre line, and no square elsewhere; each join and output feed with one Route.Config envelope of 3.0 mm or less, at most five routes and its other routes 4.0 mm or shorter; a straight input feed with no envelope; three skew measurements, each within 1.0 ps; no unmet signal measurement, unsquiggled or unrealized route, or unfound path

COMPLETION.md sorts the points the layout fixes by geometry (the jack pads, the cell port pads, the RoutePoints on each port's axis, the tangency squares; the bend RoutePoints may go here or with the designer-placed points, with a reason, since the prompt gives their place only as one that works) from what it leaves to the router (each matched middle route within its envelope), and says why each fixed point is fixed, including why the envelope route starts clear of the squares

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (the OverlappableCopper body, its pour keepout, the region fence and the resistor keepout, the fenced lines, the tangent exits and squares, the cell drawn once in WilkinsonCell, the envelope sections and the timing constraint), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.

COMPLETION.md reports the arm lengths, the pour's distance to each body, the region fence vias by row, the exit straightness, the bends and the gap to each square, and the skews as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the arm length, the body shape, the fence or the matching as validated RF performance; the numbers are the prompt's and the structure labels' and no field solve backs them
